keyVerseText: The children of Shephatiah, the children of Hattil, the children of Pochereth of Zebaim, the children of Ami. Ami: or, Amon
rootMeaning: The root of אָמִי (ʼÂmîy) is an abbreviated form of אָמוֹן (ʼÂmôwn), which means "skilled workman" or "master workman." This etymology reveals a connection to craftsmanship and service, highlighting a role of skilled labor or dedicated service rather than merely a personal name. The literal sense enriches the understanding of אָמִי beyond a simple proper name, implying a heritage linked to diligent work and faithful service within the community.
usageInScripture: The word אָמִי occurs only once in Scripture, specifically in Ezra 2:57, where it is used as a proper name referring to a group identified as the children of Ami. The top translation "of Ami" indicates a familial or tribal association, consistent with the lexicon's identification of אָמִי as a masculine proper name linked to an Israelite lineage. This singular occurrence underscores its specialized use as a personal or family name rather than a common noun or descriptive title.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding אָמִי as rooted in a term for a skilled or master workman enriches the theological appreciation of God’s people as those called to faithful service and diligent labor in His kingdom. The connection to a servant of Solomon emphasizes the biblical theme of stewardship and submission under God’s authority. From a Christ-centered perspective, this highlights the believer’s identity as one who serves under the Lord’s sovereign rule, reflecting Christ’s example of humble service and mastery over all creation. Recognizing such names in Scripture reminds believers of their calling to contribute faithfully within the body of Christ, honoring God through their gifts and heritage.
keyVerseReflection: Ezra 2:57 lists "the children of Ami," identifying a specific family group among the returning exiles. The mention that "Ami" may also be read as "Amon" links this name to a known servant of Solomon, grounding this group in a heritage of faithful service. This word contributes to the verse by highlighting the continuity of God’s people through generations marked by faithful labor and covenant identity, encouraging readers to see themselves as part of this ongoing story of God’s redemptive work.
